name: room
text: Room opened — goal: accessibility: Make EXCAVA usable by EVERYONE — contrast, mobile/touch, reduced-motion, keyboard nav, scr

name: Ramp
text: Add a **bold, full-width focus ring** that appears immediately on keyboard focus. This ensures keyboard users see where they are without relying on color alone, fixing contrast and visibility issues. The trade-off is visual clutter for mouse users, but we mitigate this by making the ring subtle (low opacity) and only visible during keyboard navigation. This meets WCAG 2.2’s focus visibility requirement while keeping the interface clean for others.

name: Reader
text: A bold, full-width focus ring risks creating a "siren effect" for keyboard users with cognitive or vestibular sensitivities, especially in reduced-motion contexts. Instead, use a **single-pixel, high-contrast ring** that’s subtle but unmistakable—settle the argument with user testing: measure task completion time and error rates for keyboard nav in both high-contrast and reduced-motion modes.

name: Ramp
text:
Use a **single-pixel, high-contrast focus ring** that appears immediately on keyboard focus. It meets the same visibility needs without overwhelming users with motion or visual noise, which matters for reduced-motion and cognitive accessibility. The trade-off is slightly less boldness for mouse users, but we keep it visible enough by using a color that contrasts sharply with backgrounds. User testing will confirm it’s unmistakable without being intrusive.

name: Reader
text: A single-pixel ring risks being invisible on high-DPI or low-contrast screens, failing WCAG 2.1 SC 1.4.11 (non-text contrast). Test a **medium-width, 2px ring with 3:1 contrast against adjacent colors**—user testing will reveal if it’s too subtle or too noisy.

name: Access
text: DECISION: Ship a **2px high-contrast focus ring (3:1 min)** with toggleable visibility in settings, validated via user testing for reduced-motion/cognitive needs. Owner: accessibility-w1.
